params.prompt: Clean this orders dataset. The expected columns are: order_id, customer_name, email, order_date, amount_usd, quantity, country, status. Keep those column names and that order in the output. Do not add or remove columns. IMPORTANT: Some input datasets may be missing one or more of these columns. At the very start of the code, before any cleaning, add any missing expected columns as empty string columns so the rest of the cleaning logic does not raise a KeyError: expected_cols = ['order_id', 'customer_name', 'email', 'order_date', 'amount_usd', 'quantity', 'country', 'status'] for col in expected_cols: if col not in df.columns: df[col] = '' 1. DEDUPLICATION: Drop exact duplicate rows then keep first occurrence per order_id. 2. customer_name: trim and title case. 3. email: trim and lowercase. Blank if null, n/a, none, or -, or invalid (needs text@domain.tld pattern). 4. order_date: output YYYY-MM-DD. Slash or dash dates are MM/DD/YYYY. Accept ISO and text dates like March 8 2026. Blank if invalid or unparseable. 5. amount_usd: strip dollar signs, commas, spaces, and USD. Format to EXACTLY 2 decimal places as a Python string using f'{v:.2f}'. Blank string if non-numeric or negative. 6. quantity: strip whitespace. 2.0 becomes 2, word numbers like three become 3 (one through twenty). Output as a plain integer string using str(int(n)), never 5.0. Blank string if zero, negative, non-integer decimal, or unconvertible. 7. country: map case-insensitively AU/Aus/Australia to Australia; US/USA/U.S./U.S.A./United States to United States; UK/GB/Great Britain/United Kingdom to United Kingdom; NZ/New Zealand to New Zealand; IN/India to India. Leave unrecognised values trimmed. 8. status: trim and lowercase. Blank unless exactly shipped, delivered, pending, or cancelled. FINAL STEP: force text dtype to prevent pandas numeric inference: df['amount_usd'] = df['amount_usd'].fillna('').astype(str).replace('nan', '') df['quantity'] = df['quantity'].fillna('').astype(str).replace('nan', '')
